sources.title: Guide to visiting the Shanghai Tower Observation Deck
sources.content:
Shanghai Tower is China's tallest building and the world's second-tallest, surpassed only by Burj Khalifa. The observation deck, called "Top of Shanghai," officially opened to the public on April 27, 2017.

Visitors can access the 118th floor (546m) and 119th floor (552m). "The 119th floor is not stated on admission tickets, but is accessible from 118th floor via a stairway." The 119th floor currently ranks as the world's second-highest observation deck.

Regular admission price is approximately 27 USD (180 Chinese Yuan). Foreign visitors can book online through designated platforms, receiving e-tickets via email for pickup at self-service kiosks. Cash, Alipay, or Tenpay payment methods are accepted at ticket halls; credit cards cannot be used.

Operating hours are 8:30 am to 10:00 pm with last entry at 9:30 pm. The tower is located at 479 Lujiazui Ring Road or 501 Yincheng Middle Road in the Pudong district.

Take subway Line 2 to Lujiazui station, exit 6. Alternatively, a ferry crossing costs only 2 Yuan, followed by a 10-minute walk.

The highest speed of the elevator is 18 meters per second, reaching the observation deck in only 55 seconds.

The 1,000+ square-meter annular platform offers 360-degree views including the Bund, Oriental Pearl Tower, Suzhou River, and neighboring skyscrapers.

Facilities: Souvenir store on 118th floor. Washing rooms available. Sky post office (world's highest). Wishing tree (cards cost 18 Yuan). 119th floor coffee shop (weekends only). Paid telescopes by windows.

Visitor Tips: Visit during dusk to see both day and night views. Bring your own telescope. Choose clear weather for optimal visibility. Visit at night during poor weather for city light visibility. Book tickets in advance for discounts and reduced wait times. Plan for 5-30 minute elevator queue times.

sources.title: Shanghai Tower Travel Guide (2026): Things to See, Do & Views
sources.content:
The Shanghai Tower stands as China's tallest building at 632 meters, ranking third globally. Construction spanned from November 2008 to March 2016, featuring 127 above-ground floors plus 5 below.

Location: 501 Yincheng Middle Road, Lujiazui, Pudong. Hours: 8:30 AM - 10:00 PM daily (last tickets at 9:30 PM). Visit Duration: Approximately 2 hours. Ticket Price: 180 RMB (adults); 90 RMB (children 1.0-1.4m); 120 RMB (seniors 60+).

The spiral architecture symbolizes modern China's rapid growth, drawing inspiration from the winding Huangpu River. The structure incorporates blurred spaces influenced by traditional Shanghai shikumen courtyards, reimagined vertically.

Top of Shanghai Observation Deck (118th Floor): Features panoramic 360-degree city views with photo opportunities including the Sky Mirror, Locks of the Heart, and Sky Post Office.

Café in the Clouds (119th Floor): Offers afternoon tea sets with sweets, sandwiches, and specialty teas at 552 meters elevation, plus Western-style dinner options with city views.

1,000-Ton Tuned Mass Damper (126th Floor): An engineering marvel described as the world's largest and heaviest dampers, stabilizing the tower against wind forces.

Luggage storage available at first-floor ticket office and B2 underground corridor. Strollers permitted, though elevator space is limited during peak hours.

Transportation: Metro Lines 2 or 14 (Lujiazui Station), buses 455/85/774/779/798/799/971/992, or ferry from East Zhongshan Road terminal.

sources.title: How to Visit Shanghai Tower - China Travel Tips
sources.content:
Shanghai Tower stands as a remarkable 632-meter structure featuring 125 stories above ground and 5 below. Its distinctive spiraling design includes double outer glass walls and represents a green, human and Knowledge skyscraper. The tower ranks as the world's second-tallest building.

Address: No. 501 Yincheng Middle Road, Pudong District. By Subway: Take Line 2 to Lujiazui station, exit 6, then walk southwest toward the tower. By Bus: Routes 583, 939, and 799 stop at Dongtai Road Station.

Purchase tickets at the Shanghai Summit ticketing office on the northwest side. The entry fee is 180 yuan per person.

Visitors descend to basement level B1 for an interactive activities exhibition hall, then proceed to B2 to access the fastest elevator and get to the 536-meter 118th floor in 55 seconds. The tower's elevator achieves an impressive 18 meters per second—the world's fastest.

The 118th-floor observation deck, called Shanghai Summit, offers over 1,000 square meters of space with 360-degree city views through a transparent triangular design, positioned 546 meters above ground.

Nearby Landmarks: Adjacent structures include Jinmao Tower (421 meters) to the north and Shanghai Global Financial Center (492 meters) to the east.

sources.title: Choosing a Shanghai Observation Deck: Comparison and Tips
sources.content:
Shanghai Tower is China's tallest building and the world's third highest structure. The observation deck sits on the 118th floor. Price: 180 yuan for 118th floor, 268 – 118th plus 126th Floor Damper Show.

Visitors can purchase tickets either on-site or through online platforms like Trip.com and Klook to avoid queuing.

The tower offers a bird's eye view over the whole city with quite convenient access and fewer crowds compared to Oriental Pearl Tower. The elevator itself is described as visually striking.

Despite impressive photography opportunities, the author found two limitations: the absence of an outdoor observation area and lack of a glass floor experience, which reduced its appeal compared to alternatives.

While Shanghai Tower provides the highest vantage point and clearest city views, visitors seeking interactive height experiences like glass floors or outdoor exposure may find other options more satisfying.

sources.title: 玩轉世界第三高樓！2026上海中心大廈旅遊攻略
sources.content:
上海中心大厦是位于上海浦东陆家嘴的一座超高层地标性建筑，建筑总高度632米，是目前中国第一高、世界第二高的摩天大楼。

门票价格：成人票180元，学生/老人票120元，儿童票90元（1.0-1.4米之间，1米以下免票）。

游玩亮点：
1. 观光厅：118层的上海之巅观光厅提供360度俯瞰上海的壮丽景观，海拔高达556米
2. 世界最快电梯：大厦拥有获得吉尼斯世界纪录认证的全世界最快速的电梯——上海中心OB3电梯，最高时速可达20.5米/秒，55秒后即可直达546米高空
3. 展览与体验：「生长的天际线」展区通过动画影片展现了从1840年到现代的上海城市发展史，「摩天梦」展区展示了从1885年以来的世界最高建筑演变

交通信息：搭乘上海地铁2号线至【陆家嘴站】，出站后步行10分钟即可到达。与金茂大厦、上海环球金融中心共同构成了上海著名的天际线。

sources.title: 上海中心大厦_百度百科
sources.content:
上海中心大厦（Shanghai Tower），位于上海市陆家嘴金融贸易区银城中路501号，是上海市的一座巨型高层地标式摩天大楼，现为中国第一高楼、世界第三高楼，始建于2008年11月29日，于2016年3月12日完成建筑总体的施工工作。

上海中心大厦主要用途为办公、酒店、商业、观光等公共设施；主楼为地上127层，建筑高度632米，地下室有5层；裪楼共7层，其中地上5层，地下2层，建筑高度为38米；总建筑面积约为57.8万平方米，其中地上总面积约41万平方米，地下总面积约16.8万平方米，占地面积30368平方米。

2013年8月3日，上海中心大厦完成主体结构最后一根钢梁的吊装工作，实现主体结构封顶，并按计划达到125层、580米的高度。2017年4月26日，上海中心大厦第118层的上海之巅观光厅对外开放。

观光门票199元/人。开放时间：08:30-21:00。

sources.title: Shanghai Tower (2026) - All You MUST Know Before You Go
sources.content:
Shanghai Tower stands at 632 meters, making it the tallest building in China and the third tallest in the world. High-speed elevators reach a speed of 18 meters per second, whisking visitors to the 118th floor's Top of Shanghai observation deck in just 55 seconds.

The Top of Shanghai Observation Deck is located on the 118th floor and provides panoramic views of Shanghai's vibrant skyline. The deck features photo spots such as the Sky Mirror for reflection photos, Locks of the Heart symbolizing romance, and the Sky Post Office where you can send a unique postcard with a special stamp.

Best Time to Go: Choose a clear day to visit as the visibility will be good. If you have to visit on a day of bad weather, nighttime is recommended as the cityscape will still be visible.

Getting There: Take the underground passage from Lujiazui Metro Station Exit 6, which connects directly to the tower's B2 level.

Queuing time depends on the number of visitors, usually taking about 5 to 10 minutes, but can take up to half an hour on holidays and weekends.

Luggage storage is available at the first-floor ticket office and the underground shopping corridor on B2. Recommended sightseeing time is 2-4 hours.
